title: Feature experiment observability lifecycle playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook describes the minimal and recommended observability artifacts for running feature-level experiments and rollouts (canary, A/B, dark launches). Intended audience: product owners, feature engineers, oncall, and observability engineers.

Scope
- Experiments that interact with inference endpoints, routing, caching, or model selection.
- Focus on signals needed to detect regressions in latency, correctness, and cost impact.
- Not a replacement for full model onboarding checklist.

Definitions and signal maturity
We track metric maturity in three tiers: proto, verified, contract.
- proto: quick ad-hoc counters or probes for early experiments. Low retention, low SLAs.
- verified: instrumented with schema and basic dashboards; enough to validate behaviour under load.
- contract: stable metric with ownership, documented SLA, included in SLOs and runbooks.

Minimum metric set for a feature experiment (proto -> verified target)
- experiment_request_count: counter tagged by experiment_id, route, model_variant. proto: 1m retention, verified: 90d.
- experiment_success_rate: percent success per experiment_id. success defined by 200 response and non-empty body.
- median_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms: per-route, per-model. Use request duration downstream of the routing decision.
- token_cost_estimate: approximate tokens * per-token unit from billing. Useful to surface runaway costs from prompts.
- kvcache_hit_rate: per-tenant, per-experiment when experiment touches prefix cache.
- output_quality_fallback_rate: events where fallback model or heuristic was used.
- error_kind_count: counter with labels error_category, experiment_id (proto: coarse categories, verified: structured error codes).

Metric tagging guidance
- experiment_id: required for all experiment signals. Short readable id.
- route: logical API route.
- model_family and model_variant: allow grouping.
- tenant_id: where applicable; if PII, use hashed id.

Tracing plan and sampling by phase
Phases: dev -> staging -> canary -> scale. Sampling adapts to phase to balance signal and cost.
- dev: tracing off by default; use on-demand full traces via debug flag. Sample rate 0.1% for baseline.
- staging: sample 1% of requests, 100% for test runs. Ensure span names include experiment_id and routing decision span.
- canary (initial 1-5% traffic): sample 10% of canary traffic, 100% for errors and fallback flows.
- scale: sample 1-2% globally; retain 100% of error traces and 100% of traces that hit fallback or model downgrade.

Trace annotations required
- experiment_id tag on root span.
- routing_decision span with selected model_variant and reason code.
- kvcache_lookup span with cache_key and result (hit/miss). Keep keys redacted.
- billing_estimate span showing estimated tokens and cost bucket.

Trace budget heuristics (example numbers)
- target trace retention for experiment period: 30 days of sampled traces. For a busy route this means sample rate adjustments to stay under trace store budget.
- cost rule of thumb: 100k traces roughly equals 1.2 GB compressed storage per month. Use this when approving long-running experiments.

Dashboard and microdash guidance
- Every experiment should have a lightweight microdash (single-row) visible in the rollout dashboard: request rate, success rate, p95, cost estimate, kvcache_heatmap, error trend.
- Template widgets: small sparkline for trend, current value, change vs baseline percent.
- Baseline comparison: show experiment cohort vs control cohort and global baseline. Use consistent color palette where control = gray, experiment = blue.
- Alert panels: avoid noisy thresholds in proto. For verified level, add alert if p95 regresses by >25% and error_rate increases by >2x vs baseline for 15m.

Rollout readiness checklist (pre-canary)
- Instrumentation present for minimum metrics and tracing anchors.
- Microdash auto-created (use telemetry templates).
- Owner assigned and oncall informed for initial canary window.
- Linked experiment definition in Jira/Confluence with expected traffic ramp.

Investigation playbook (when anomaly detected)
1. Confirm scope using microdash: tenant vs global, model_variant, route.
2. Pull traces for impacted experiment_id and time window. Look for routing changes, kvcache eviction, or model selection fallback.
3. If cost spike: check token_cost_estimate and prompt length distribution.
4. If quality regressions: pull output examples, annotate, and compare to control.
5. If systemic latency: check backend platform metrics (GPU utilization, queueing, batching). Link to infra SRE runbook.

Automation and ownership
- Owner: feature engineering team must own experiment_id tag and local metric definitions.
- Observability: eng-observability owns templates, sampling knobs, dashboards, and runbook scaffolds.
- SRE: owns escalation channels and resource throttling during burst experiments.

Examples and quick queries
- Simple availability query: sum(increase(experiment_success_rate{experiment_id=~"exp-.*"}[5m])) by (experiment_id) / sum(increase(experiment_request_count{experiment_id=~"exp-.*"}[5m])) by (experiment_id)
- p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket{experiment_id="exp-42"}[5m])) by (le))
- kvcache heatmap: topk(10, avg_over_time(kvcache_hit_rate{experiment_id="exp-42"}[1h])) by (tenant_id)

Cost and retention proposals
- Proto experiments: metrics retention 7 days, traces off by default.
- Verified experiments: metrics retention 90 days, traces sampled at 1-10% depending on route criticality.
- Contract signals: retention 365 days for essential SLO-related aggregates.

Templated artifacts to create for each experiment (automation recommended)
- microdash id and link inserted into experiment doc.
- experiment metric set auto-created from template (with tags).
- tracing sampling profile applied based on chosen phase.
- Slack alert channel and oncall owner assigned.

Open questions and TODOs
- Should we standardize a single experiment_id naming convention across orgs? proposal: team-code/short-slug/date.
- How to safely include hashed prompt fingerprint in traces for output quality debugging without exposing sensitive data. Explore HMAC schemes.
- Build CLI to auto-create microdash + metric templates from a simple manifest. PR tracked in linked_artifacts.

Notes to self and quick reminders
- Keep proto low-friction: avoid gating small experiments on long instrumentation work.
- Use differential metrics where possible to avoid stooping to absolute thresholds that are noisy.
- When in doubt, increase sampling for error flows rather than full sampling.

References
- internal onboarding confluence page: OBS-EXPERIMENT-LIFECYCLE.
- telemetry repo PR: telemetry/pull/452 for dashboard templating.

Contact
- Morgan Lee (owner), slack morgan.lee, pager for oncall coordination.

End of playbook.
